question: After a wedding, how long does the average boost in life satisfaction last?
answer: About two years. Following Germans for 15 years, Lucas and colleagues saw satisfaction climb around the wedding and then drift back to where it had been before. Averages hide spread: some ended happier than they began, some less happy. The new normal is still a marriage, simply no longer a new one.
move: Expect the glow of any big change to fade; plan for the ordinary days after.
ask: Which change am I counting on to make me lastingly happier, and what will it feel like after two years?
reference: Lucas, Clark, Georgellis & Diener, Reexamining adaptation and the set point model of happiness: reactions to changes in marital status, Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 2003
